title: U.S. House · Illinois's 15th District
area: East-central and southeastern Illinois, including Danville, Mattoon, and Centralia.

context.text: Incumbent Mary Miller defeated Ryan Tebrugge and Judy Bowlby in the March 17, 2026 Republican primary, 73.6% to 14.8% to 11.6%. Jennifer Todd defeated Paul Davis, Randy Raley, and Kyle Nudo in the Democratic primary, 45.7% to 33.7% to 11.4% to 9.1%.

candidates.name: Mary Miller
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 17, 2026 Republican primary with 73.6% of the vote

summary.text: Mary Miller is the Republican U.S. Representative for Illinois's 15th District, first elected in 2020. A former teacher who, with her husband, farms in Illinois, she serves on the Agriculture, Education and Workforce, and House Administration committees. She is seeking a fourth term.

background.text: Born in Oak Park, Illinois, in 1959. According to Wikipedia, she graduated from Naperville Central High School.

Graduated from Eastern Illinois University with a B.S. in business management and completed graduate coursework in education, earning an Illinois teaching certification, according to her official biography.

Her career experience includes work as a farmer, business manager and teacher. Her official biography says she and her husband Chris raised seven children on the family farm, and her campaign website describes her as a former Sunday school teacher.
Ran in 2020 to succeed retiring Rep. John Shimkus, won the Republican nomination, and defeated Democrat Erika Weaver in the general election. Her campaign website says she received 73.4% of the vote.
Took office in January 2021. In the 2022 redistricting cycle she won the Republican primary against fellow incumbent Rep. Rodney Davis (per Wikipedia); she was unopposed in the 2024 general election.
Won the March 17, 2026 Republican primary with 73.6% over Ryan Tebrugge and Judy Bowlby.

Serves on the House Agriculture, Education and Workforce, and House Administration committees, is a member of the House Freedom Caucus and Republican Study Committee, and in March 2023 founded the Congressional Family Caucus, which she chairs.
Her official biography says she and her husband have 23 grandchildren.

priorities.text: Says that on the House Agriculture Committee she serves as a voice for small family farmers, working across the aisle to fund crop insurance and pass rural broadband legislation.

Says she is a member of the House Freedom Caucus and Republican Study Committee, where she fights for "conservative, Constitutional principles including the Right to Life, the Second Amendment, and ballot security."

positions.summary: Says she has opposed the Biden administration's "red-flag" gun measures and identifies as a strong supporter of Second Amendment rights.
positions.quote: Mary is the only member of Congress from Illinois to oppose every aspect of the Biden-Pelosi agenda, including the disgraceful January 6th “witch hunt” Commission, President Biden’s “red-flag” gun confiscation measures, COVID vaccine mandates and databases, and taxpayer-funded chemical abortion.

positions.summary: Opposed the Green New Deal by name, saying it would raise fuel costs and impoverish rural families.
positions.quote: The Green New Deal would raise the cost of motor fuel and would impoverish rural families. Mary Miller will fight to protect rural residents by opposing radical ideas like the Green New Deal.

positions.summary: Her 2020 campaign website said she supports building a wall on the southern border and supports the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency, while opposing sanctuary cities.
positions.quote: Mary Miller OPPOSES sanctuary cities and she SUPPORTS building a wall on our southern border and she SUPPORTS the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the Joint Committee on the Library, the Committee on Agriculture (Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture; Conservation, Research and Biotechnology; General Farm Commodities, Risk Management and Credit; Livestock, Dairy and Poultry), and the Committee on Education and the Workforce.

Introduced legislation to stop the EPA from applying Waters of the United States (WOTUS) regulations to farmers and ranchers, and sponsored legislation to stop foreign entities, including China, from buying U.S. farmland.
Sponsored legislation to allow whole milk back into the school lunch program and worked on rural broadband legislation as a member of the House Agriculture Committee.

candidates.name: Jennifer Todd
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary with 45.7% of the vote in a four-way field

summary.text: Jennifer Todd is the Democratic nominee for Illinois's 15th Congressional District and a nurse and small business owner from Edwardsville. She won a four-way Democratic primary in March 2026 and is making her first run against incumbent Republican Mary Miller.

background.text: Born in Illinois and graduated from Centralia High School.
Earned an associate degree from Kaskaskia Community College and bachelor's degrees from Southern Illinois University Edwardsville and Southern Illinois University Carbondale.
Her career experience includes working as a nurse and small business owner; NPR Illinois / St. Louis Public Radio describes her as an Edwardsville nurse.
Won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary with 45.7% of the vote over Paul Davis, Randy Raley and Kyle Nudo.

In the primary she presented herself as someone who understands working-class struggles, having used Medicaid, the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program and unemployment benefits. She lives in Edwardsville, less than a mile outside the district, and told the outlet she would move to Logan County if elected.

researchNotes: Jennifer Todd has not completed the 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and no campaign-website issue positions were located for her within the research budget for this race. Mary Miller's official house.gov issues pages (marymiller.house.gov/issues) contain only press-release feeds with no issue statements; her current campaign "About" page and her archived 2020 campaign website (reproduced on her Ballotpedia page) were used instead for positions on immigration enforcement, which is not restated on her current site. Miller's Ballotpedia profile says she earned a second bachelor's degree in elementary education while her official biography says graduate coursework in education, so the official version is used; Todd's prior public offices, if any, were not found.
